transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-30 08:00 PT / 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Emily Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Redwood Solutions), Laura Miles (Scion Head of Data), Omar Reyes (Scion Platform Eng), Sofia Kim (Scion Security), Ben Carter (Scion ML)

Summary: quick alignment on POC goals, gather traffic and token stats, agree bench plan and timeline

00:00:02 Emily Chen: thanks everyone for joining, we'll keep this tight, main goal is to size the POC and agree success criteria and what we need from you, no surprises
00:00:18 Laura Miles: yeah thanks, appreciate it. we want to run a 4-week POC to validate latency and cost for our conversational assistant and a nightly batch ingestion flow, so two workload classes
00:00:35 Ravi Patel: perfect. can you describe qps patterns, peak concurrency and typical input/output sizes for both flows? even ballpark numbers help a lot
00:00:49 Ben Carter: sure, for the assistant we see roughly 3 qps steady during business hours, peaks of maybe 25 qps during marketing campaigns; concurrency per user session is low but concurrent sessions can hit 60 at peak. inputs average around 120 tokens, outputs average 90 tokens but sometimes go to 400 tokens on long responses
00:01:15 Omar Reyes: the batch job is separate: once per night ingest pipeline calls an embedder and summarizer, it's about 2000 requests in a 30 minute window, so roughly 1 qps average during that slot but with bursts, and token sizes vary - long docs 2k tokens input, but outputs are shorter summaries ~300 tokens
00:01:42 Maya Lopez: quick clarifying q: when you say 25 qps peak, is that sustained over minutes or a short burst under a minute?
00:01:51 Ben Carter: usually short bursts, 2-5 minutes during promo, but we have seen sustained 10-15 qps for an hour on heavy days
00:02:05 Ravi Patel: ok that helps. for sizing we typically look at p95 and p99 latency objectives, target throughput, and the token distribution tail since memory/KV cache and batch sizing change with sequence length
00:02:22 Laura Miles: our success criteria are mainly: 95th percentile latency under 350 ms for interactive flows, throughput to handle peaks without queueing, and cost that doesn't blow our forecast - we have a target of under $0.002 per generated token on average but can be flexible if latency is much better
00:02:44 Emily Chen: that's clear. we should capture test cases: short assist (input 30-80 tokens, output 20-80 tokens), typical assist (input 80-160 tokens, output 60-150 tokens), long response (input 200-600 tokens, output up to 400 tokens), and batch doc summarize (input 1500-2500 tokens, output 200-400 tokens). we'll map those to qps profiles you gave
00:03:09 Sofia Kim: on security, we'll need SOC2 + encryption at rest, KMS integration, and an audit log for inference requests. also any private deployment options for regulated data?
00:03:24 Emily Chen: Redwood has hosted, dedicated and private options. for this POC we can run hosted but with VPC peering and customer-managed KMS if needed; private on-prem would be a later phase. we'll share SOC2 docs and network diagram after the call
00:03:41 Ravi Patel: getting back to traffic, could you share sample logs for 7 days? we use those to build a synthetic load shape and pick test points - steady, diurnal, and peak bursts. that'll feed our benchmarking harness and the model variants we recommend
00:03:58 Omar Reyes: yes we can share logs - we'll sanitize and drop PII before sending. timeline-wise we want POC to start first week of April if possible
00:04:10 Emily Chen: good, so plan: you send logs by Friday, we build traffic model and propose VM/GPU sizing and a bench plan, run benchmark and share results. typical turnaround is ~1 week to get initial sizing and a 2-week benchmark window if we run multiple model variants
00:04:28 Ben Carter: curious about model variants - are you recommending quantized models for cost savings? any hit on latency?
00:04:36 Ravi Patel: yes we routinely use int8/int4 quantized variants for throughput and cost; sometimes int4 can increase latency slightly if kernel paths aren't optimal, but on modern runtimes it's usually neutral or even better because reduced memory bandwidth helps. we'll recommend per-case: for short interactions lower precision often works, for long-context summarization we might prefer fp16 or 8-bit that preserves quality
00:05:00 Maya Lopez: also worth noting we'll propose batching settings and prefix caching. for the assistant we can enable prefix KV caching for repeated session context which reduces compute for back-and-forth dialog
00:05:11 Laura Miles: ok, what metrics will you run in the bench? p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, cost per token, and accuracy/regression on a sample prompt set?
00:05:21 Emily Chen: exactly. we'll measure latency percentiles, throughput (tokens/sec), concurrency behaviors under realistic session shaping, and a small evaluation suite for quality regression. we'll record logs and provide a spreadsheet with cost calculations.
00:05:36 Ravi Patel: small note: sometimes transcripts call out KV cache as K-B cache in our exported logs - ignore that if you see it, it's just the ASR mis-hearing. also we may have model names munged in the transcript e.g., 'red wood' instead of Redwood
00:05:50 Ben Carter: ha, noted. on the quality deck, we'd want a threshold for acceptable generation quality - maybe 90% pass rate on a set of 50 prompts for intent correctness?
00:06:02 Sofia Kim: from security side, if we're using hosted with VPC peering we need private egress routes, and all inference logs must be encrypted and retained for 90 days. is that supported?
00:06:15 Emily Chen: yes supported as add-on; we can map retention and export hooks to your SIEM. we'll include that in the doc we share
00:06:26 Omar Reyes: one practical question on the load testing: we usually drive session-oriented synthetic workloads rather than stateless bursts. can you simulate sessions with KV caching to see real benefits?
00:06:38 Ravi Patel: absolutely - we'll model session stickiness and prefix caching. we'll include both cold-cache and warm-cache runs since cold startup is relevant for scale-up behavior
00:06:50 Laura Miles: timeline check: if you can get the sizing doc in a week we can sign the SOW and start the POC in the week of April 6. any blockers?
00:07:02 Emily Chen: blockers would be access to logs and any strict network requirements; otherwise it's straightforward
00:07:08 Ben Carter: question on concurrency: when you report concurrency can you map it to GPU saturation and expected latencies? we need guidance like '2x A100 equivalent for 25 qps on model X with avg 120 tokens in/out'
00:07:22 Ravi Patel: yes we'll provide a hardware mapping table: model variant, memory footprint, expected qps per GPU at target latency, and suggested redundancy for headroom. note these are estimates; bench runs will give precise numbers
00:07:35 Maya Lopez: we'll also include a failure mode plan - what happens when capacity is saturated, fallback to cheaper model variant or region routing?
00:07:44 Emily Chen: Redwood supports automatic fallback to smaller model variants and routing policies; we can demo that in a follow-up
00:07:52 Sofia Kim: legal will ask about data residency - if PII is present in logs we need to know whether Redwood persists any of that in hosted mode
00:08:03 Emily Chen: by default hosted logs are retained for diagnostics but can be turned off; for regulated data we recommend Dedicated or Private where you control retention. we'll document retention options in the security packet
00:08:18 Laura Miles: ok, let's walk through an example bench point: baseline interactive profile, 5 qps sustained, 25 qps peak bursts for 3 minutes, input median 120, output median 80 tokens. what would you run?
00:08:33 Ravi Patel: for that we'd run a staged benchmark: cold-cache ramp from 1 qps to 5 qps, measure p50/p95/p99, then inject bursts to 25 qps with session shaping, measure queueing and autoscale reaction, and run quality eval on a 100 prompt sample. we'd also run long-tail tests with 400 token outputs to measure memory pressure
00:08:55 Ben Carter: how do you model cost? is it per-token for hosted and per-GPU-hour for dedicated?
00:09:03 Emily Chen: hosted is typically measured as a blended per-token + infra surcharge; in the bench we'll estimate cost per generated token using observed tokens/sec and runtime pricing. for Dedicated we'll show per-GPU cost and amortized per-token cost for your traffic profile
00:09:18 Omar Reyes: do you support multi-model routing? we want cheaper model for low-risk queries and a higher-quality model for escalation
00:09:25 Ravi Patel: yes, policy-based routing is supported. we can simulate multi-model routing in the POC and show cost/latency tradeoffs on the dashboard
00:09:36 Laura Miles: let's capture acceptance criteria in plain language: 1) interactive 95th < 350ms on typical prompts, 2) no request failures at 25 qps bursts beyond a small bounded retry window, 3) avg cost below $0.002 per generated token for steady state, 4) security checklist completed.
00:09:55 Emily Chen: agreed. we'll include quantifiable pass/fail points in the test plan. any additions?
00:10:05 Sofia Kim: add proof of KMS integration and log export during POC as a security gate
00:10:11 Emily Chen: noted
00:10:18 Maya Lopez: for the workload model we'll produce a traffic shape file with percentiles: peak 99.9th, p99, p95, and average. we'll also provide recommended batching and qps per GPU numbers
00:10:31 Ben Carter: if you need sample prompts for quality tests we can hand off a set of 200 prioritized prompts, annotated with expected intents
00:10:40 Emily Chen: perfect. who owns the initial data handoff? Laura?
00:10:44 Laura Miles: yes me and Ben will drop the logs and prompt set into the secure share by Wednesday
00:10:52 Ravi Patel: cool. then our immediate deliverables: traffic model + sizing doc (ETA 1 week), bench plan & test matrix (ETA 1 week), security packet (SOC2/KMS/network) today or tomorrow, and then we schedule kickoff April 6
00:11:08 Omar Reyes: one more nit - for long-doc summarization, do you recommend chunking or long-context models?
00:11:16 Ravi Patel: depends. chunking with an external reranker and stitching pipeline sometimes is more cost effective, but for higher-quality single-pass summaries long-context models avoid coherence issues. we'll test both strategies in the POC
00:11:30 Ben Carter: great. about reporting: can you break down token cost by input vs output? our finance wants clear line items
00:11:38 Emily Chen: yes the cost spreadsheet will show input token cost, output token cost, infra amortization and per-request overheads
00:11:46 Sofia Kim: and include where the logs are stored and retention settings so we can map to our compliance needs
00:11:53 Emily Chen: will do
00:12:00 Laura Miles: ok unless there are other big items let's recap next steps
00:12:05 Emily Chen: recap: Scion provides 7-day traffic logs and prompt set by 2027-03-31; Redwood sends benchmark template, traffic model, and security packet by 2027-04-01; schedule POC kickoff for 2027-04-06; run bench and share results in two weeks. action owners captured in the deck.
00:12:28 Omar Reyes: sounds good
00:12:31 Maya Lopez: I'll also include a proposed hardware table and model variant recommendations with caveats
00:12:38 Ben Carter: thanks all, look forward to it
00:12:41 Emily Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via calendar invite and upload docs to the shared folder
00:12:46 Transcript ends.
